Swapped to $open (also raw) to remove the artifact. Left untouched, the denominator ADD(TS_RANK($dollar_volume,5),1e-8) would stay byte-identical to the archived parent, and af43733e's own admission rationale already calls further renormalization of this denominator a dead end (rho 0.92+) with 5/10/21/63 all now saturated in archive+rejections, so pushed the window to an untested 126 instead of a same-family retune.

Same dividend-adjusted-close/raw-low scale mix as af43733e's numerator, on this island's seed formula. A rejected mutation on this exact chassis (TS_MIN($low,5) over TS_MAX($high,42)-TS_MIN($low,42)) already shows a window-only retune still correlates at rho 0.875 against this parent, so a plain window change alone is not enough. Paired the $close->$open fix with a mismatched TS_MAX window (21->10, distinct from the already-rejected 5/42 combination) so the denominator isn't left byte-identical either.

Same numerator scale-mix issue as af43733e (this formula is c0a5abed's own admitted mutation of the same 9b349c02 parent). TS_STD($close,w) is already saturated at w=5/10/21/63 across archive and rejections, so kept the field but moved to an untested 126-day window alongside the $close->$open numerator fix, avoiding a verbatim restatement of the untouched denominator.

ABS(EPS) discards the sign of earnings, scoring a large loss as if it were an equally strong profit. MAX(EPS,0) keeps the profit-magnitude signal for the majority of (profitable) names but collapses all loss-makers to a single tied floor instead of rewarding bigger losses as 'stronger', fixing the sign-blind weak component directly.

This lineage's sibling mutation (8f76527f, itself a child of this parent) documents that smoothing/shifting the $close denominator is a dead end here (TS_MEAN($close,5) was a within-run duplicate, TS_MEAN($close,21) hit rho 0.998) and that only a non-monotonic transform of EPS decorrelates. ABS(EPS) is already taken by 8f76527f and EPS/book_per_share variants are already archived, so used the complementary MIN(EPS,0) loss-floor (untested) instead of ABS's magnitude fold, targeting the same bare-EPS weak component with a distinct, non-monotonic lever.

candidates.rationale: Same numerator scale-mix fix as af43733e ($close -> $open), applied at the root of this family. 9b349c02's own admission rationale already calls further window/denominator tweaks on raw $dollar_volume a known dead end; log-compressing the heavy-tailed volume divisor is a fresh, untested lever (0 hits in archive/rejections) distinct from the smoothing/ranking already ruled out, and it only adds one wrapper node so the epsilon-guard block stays small enough to dodge archive_subtree.

Working-memory rule 5 flags TS_DELTA($close,w) as a repeatedly-failing weak leg (4x cheap_screen failures) while TS_DELTA($volume,3) is the proven substitute 'delta ingredient' behind two accepts. Swapped both $close references in the normalized delta leg to $volume; the added /( $volume+eps) normalization keeps this distinct (7 vs 4 nodes) from the already-archived bare RANK(TS_DELTA($volume,3)) sibling.

This leg's own documented child (cf8910d8) states every OHLC-anchor swap tried on this exact ratio stayed at rho>=0.85, so an anchor swap alone will not clear correlation, and wrapping the untouched 7-node ratio in TS_RANK alone would restate it verbatim (archive_subtree). Combined an anchor change ($low->$high) with a TS_RANK(...,21) wrapper, converting the bare same-day ratio into a 21-day percentile -- the same kind of added temporal structure that cleared correlation elsewhere (rule 10's 3.713 accept) -- so the leg changes in kind, not just in which OHLC field it uses.

Bare $dollar_volume is the flagged-saturated 'X' in this EPS-rank-spread family (memory: saturated for any X, rho 0.92-1.00). TS_RANK($dollar_volume,w) is the proven fix elsewhere (rule 10's 3.713 accept), but w=5/10/21/63 are all already mined in this archive and its rejections, so used an untested 126-day window to add independent temporal variation without restating an existing sibling.

DELAY($close,1) is the most noise-sensitive component: a single stale print driving the whole ratio. Rejections show both smoothing it (TS_MEAN($close,5), rho 0.886) and a small shift bump (DELAY($close,5), rho 0.819) already fail just above the 0.80 threshold, with correlation dropping as the reference moves further from 'yesterday'. Pushed the shift substantially further to 21 to extend that same decorrelating trend rather than repeating an already-failed small tweak.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Each parent is shown with its fitness and nothing else. Fitness is a single scalar in which higher is better; it already accounts for significance, year-to-year stability, complexity and turnover. You are not given per-year, coverage, turnover or horizon diagnostics in this run, so choose the component to change from the expression itself.

  1. TS_RANK($high - $low, 63) * CS_RANK(TS_STD($volume, 21)) accepted at 4.998 with no fundamental leg at all, the round's second-best.   2. TS_CORR(ABS($return), TS_RANK($volume, 21), 21) accepted at 4.507. Rank-transforming the volume leg is what rescues a return/volume correlation; raw-return-vs-raw-volume stays a dead end, but the fix is TS_RANK on volume, not abandoning the pairing.
  3. The fundamental-minus-raw-leg rank spread set a new round-best (6.794, EPS minus a bounded price-position ratio); keep exploring bounded price ratios as the 'other' leg, not just volume/range ranks. The one spread that failed did so on coverage from a 252-day window on the non-fundamental leg, not the fundamental choice; cap any window in a spread at 63 days regardless of which leg carries it.
  4. Two crossover children were rejected for donating only 2 shared nodes from a normal 5-node parent instead of exactly 3, both against the same RANK($roa) * RANK($dollar_volume) parent, both replacing one whole branch and keeping only the other operator-plus-leaf pair. Target an exactly-3-node shared subtree with each parent, not a whole branch or a single leaf.
  5. TS_DELTA($close, w) as a standalone or multiplied-in displacement leg failed cheap_screen 4x this round (|t| 0.08-0.56, incl. ABS(TS_DELTA($close,15))/range and two CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($close,3))*... variants); TS_DELTA($volume,3) played the same 'delta ingredient' role inside 2 accepts (1.383, 0.867) instead — prefer volume deltas over close deltas.
  6. Wrapping only the volume argument of an already-archived TS_CORR(x, $volume, w) in TS_RANK does not decorrelate: TS_CORR(TS_STD($return,5), TS_RANK($volume,21), 21) hit rho 0.857 and TS_CORR(TS_RANK($volume,10), $high-$low, 10) hit rho 0.809, both against raw-$volume archive parents with different partner terms and windows.
  7. TS_STD($high-$low,63)/(TS_STD($high-$low,5)+1e-8) alone failed cheap_screen (|t| 0.86) — this vol-term-structure ratio only cleared before when crossed with a momentum/delta multiplier (prior 6.583 accept); don't resubmit the bare ratio.
  8. $return-driven kernels failed cheap_screen again this round (TS_CORR($return,...) 0.26, ABS($return)*TS_DELTA(TS_RANK($volume,...),...) 0.42) — still the weakest primary leg available.
  9. TS_RANK($high-$low,21) is archive-blocked under any outer wrapper (collided both inside a CS_RANK($accrual_gap)* product and inside a TS_CORR(...,126) with volume rank); the stochastic ($close-TS_MIN($low,21))/(X($high,21)-TS_MIN($low,21)) chassis is now closed for X = TS_MAX or EMA. Move to a different window or range statistic, not a smoothing-function swap.
  10. RANK($earnings_per_share) - RANK(TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63)) was this round's best fitness (3.713) — nesting TS_RANK inside the non-fundamental leg of a rank-spread still clears correlation against flatter versions; this template still has room.
  11. CS_RANK($roa) * TS_RANK($high-$low,5) scored 3.149 (2nd best) — short-window (5-day) range-rank crossed with a fundamental rank is still open, unlike the saturated 21/63-day range windows.
  12. 3 of 20 rejects (15%) this round were exact within-run duplicates — diff new proposals against the full batch already proposed this run, not just the archive.
